speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing dizziness, nausea, and imbalance; to help me understand the cause, please describe exactly when these symptoms started and if you have any history of head injury or high blood pressure.

speaker: Patient
text: 27-year-old male. The patient reports a sustained sensation of the room spinning since this morning, which is low grade and constant. He occasionally feels nauseous and has taken diphenhydramine to help him sleep, which also alleviates his symptoms slightly. He mentions recent increased intake of garlic due to trying to recover from a cold a few days ago. Past medical history is unremarkable.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that description. The fact that diphenhydramine helps suggests a vestibular origin, but I need to rule out central causes. Can you tell me if you experience any double vision, slurred speech, weakness on one side of your body, or trouble walking without support?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Sustained sensation of the room spinning. I also have Occasional nausea, Use of diphenhydramine for symptoms and to aid sleep, Recent cold.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV) unlikely due to sustained nature; likely Vestibular Neuritis or Labyrinthitis given recent viral illness and constant spinning vertigo relieved by diphenhydramine. No further questions needed; please proceed to treatment.
